gausser
Overview Pipeline steps Capture types Scene and state View, orbit, align, crop Monitor Command reference Architecture Troubleshooting

Reports: drone mapping, crop + adaptive, flight patterns

Command reference

Every command and option, generated from cli.build_parser(). Every command also takes -h/--help; most take -s/--scene DIR (default: the current folder), and the ones that change a scene take --monitor. What the commands are for is on the other pages.

run frames mask solve dense mesh map train lod view orbit align crop status monitor

gausser run

run every step that is missing or out of date

Run the pipeline unattended. Steps that are already up to date are skipped.

gausser run [-h] [-s SCENE] [--monitor] [--video VIDEO] [--import]
                   [--prompt PROMPT] [--dense] [--lod] [--mesh] [--map]
                   [--from {frames,mask,solve,dense,train,lod,mesh,map}]
                   [--spacing {low,medium,high}] [--min-frames MIN_FRAMES]
                   [--max-frames MAX_FRAMES] [--every N] [--overlap PERCENT]
                   [--threshold THRESHOLD] [--all-instances]
                   [--dilation DILATION] [--feather FEATHER] [--device DEVICE]
                   [--sam-checkpoint SAM_CHECKPOINT] [--miss {keep,drop}]
                   [--matcher {auto,exhaustive,sequential,spatial,vocab_tree}]
                   [--resolution-level RESOLUTION_LEVEL]
                   [--trainer {brush,msplat}] [--iterations ITERATIONS]
                   [--export-every EXPORT_EVERY] [--max-splats MAX_SPLATS]
                   [--max-resolution MAX_RESOLUTION] [--eval-split N]
                   [--adaptive] [--max-iterations MAX_ITERATIONS]
                   [--init {auto,dense,lidar,sparse}] [--downscale DOWNSCALE]
                   [--checkpoint-every CHECKPOINT_EVERY]
                   [--chunk-count CHUNK_COUNT] [--chunk-extent CHUNK_EXTENT]
                   [--levels LEVELS] [--faces FACES] [--no-refine]
                   [--texture-size TEXTURE_SIZE] [--resolution M] [--no-masks]

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
-s, --scene.scene folder (default: current folder)
--monitorwatch this command in the web monitor (`gausser monitor`)
--videoextract frames from this video first
--importfirst move photos lying in the scene folder into images/
--promptSAM3 subject prompt; without it nothing is masked
--densealso build a dense point cloud before training; Brush then starts from it
--lodalso build a streamed LOD set
--meshalso build a textured mesh (implies --dense)
--mapalso make an orthophoto and DSM (needs images with GPS)
--fromframes | mask | solve | dense | train | lod | mesh | mapredo this step and every step after it
--no-masksignore existing masks: COLMAP sees whole images, Brush and Msplat train on whole images

frames

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
--spacinglow | medium | highmediumhow far the camera moves between frames: low = fewer frames, high = more (default medium)
--min-frames150use closer spacing if fewer frames result (default 150)
--max-frames600use wider spacing if more frames result (default 600)
--everyinstead of by motion: the sharpest of every N video frames
--overlapmapping (straight-down drone video): a frame whenever the next one would share only PERCENT of the view, e.g. 80; no frame count limits. A DJI video's .SRT subtitle file gives the frames GPS

mask (SAM3)

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
--threshold0.5minimum SAM3 score (default 0.5; try 0.3 for low hit rates)
--all-instanceskeep every matching instance, not only the best
--dilationgrow Brush masks by N pixels; negative N shrinks them (edge pixels mixed with background)
--featherblur Brush mask edges by N pixels
--deviceautoauto, mps, cuda or cpu
--sam-checkpointlocal SAM3 checkpoint instead of Hugging Face
--misskeep | dropkeepwhen SAM3 finds nothing in an image: keep = train on the whole image (default); drop = Brush ignores the image, COLMAP still uses it

solve (COLMAP)

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
--matcherauto | exhaustive | sequential | spatial | vocab_treeautoauto = spatial (GPS neighbours) when most images have GPS, else exhaustive up to 200 images, else sequential with loop detection; vocab_tree suits large unordered photo sets

dense (OpenMVS)

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
--resolution-level1halve the images N times before estimating depth (default 1; 0 = full size, about 4x slower)

train

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
--trainerbrush | msplatbrushBrush (default) or the experimental Msplat
--iterations30000training steps (default 30000)
--export-every5000Brush: write a .ply every N steps
--max-splats1500000Brush: splat ceiling (default 1.5M)
--max-resolutionBrush: cap the longest image side
--eval-splitBrush: hold out every Nth image and report PSNR/SSIM on it every 1000 steps
--adaptiveBrush: after --iterations, train 5000 more steps at a time while held-out PSNR gains 0.1 dB (holds out every 20th image unless --eval-split is given)
--max-iterations60000Brush: --adaptive stops here (default 60000)
--initauto | dense | lidar | sparseautoBrush: start from the dense cloud (dense/), an iPhone scan's LiDAR points (arkit/) or COLMAP's points; auto = dense, else lidar, when there is one and Brush gets no masks
--downscale4.0Msplat: load images at 1/N size (default 4)
--checkpoint-every1000Msplat: checkpoint every N steps

gausser frames

select sharp video frames into images/

Select sharp frames into images/: one is picked wherever the camera has moved on, so a walk-around gives enough overlapping frames without tuning. A folder of photos is used whole.

gausser frames [-h] [-s SCENE] [--monitor] [--range START-END]
                      [--spacing {low,medium,high}] [--min-frames MIN_FRAMES]
                      [--max-frames MAX_FRAMES] [--every N]
                      [--overlap PERCENT]
                      source

positional arguments

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
sourcevideo file, folder of videos or images, or an iPhone LiDAR scan folder (Stray Scanner app)

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
-s, --scene.scene folder (default: current folder)
--monitorwatch this command in the web monitor (`gausser monitor`)
--rangekeep only this part of the video, in seconds or m:ss (repeatable), e.g. --range 1.5-32.5 --range 0:57-1:20

gausser dense

build a dense point cloud with OpenMVS

Estimate a depth map per image with OpenMVS (on the GPU) and fuse them into dense/scene_dense.ply. `train` then starts Brush from it, and `mesh` builds a surface from it.

gausser dense [-h] [-s SCENE] [--monitor]
                     [--resolution-level RESOLUTION_LEVEL]

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
-s, --scene.scene folder (default: current folder)
--monitorwatch this command in the web monitor (`gausser monitor`)

dense (OpenMVS)

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
--resolution-level1halve the images N times before estimating depth (default 1; 0 = full size, about 4x slower)

gausser map

orthophoto and DSM GeoTIFFs from the trained splat

Render the newest splat straight down into runs/map/<time>/: ortho.tif and dsm.tif in the scene's CRS and map.html, the orthophoto over a web map. Needs a model georeferenced from GPS (drone photos, or DJI video frames with a .SRT subtitle file).

gausser map [-h] [-s SCENE] [--monitor] [--resolution M] [source]

gausser orbit

render a 360° orbit video of a splat

Render a 360° orbit video with SuperSplat's video renderer in a browser window. Needs the scene's COLMAP model (camera path) and a Brush export (vertical axis).

gausser orbit [-h] [-s SCENE] [--seconds SECONDS] [--size SIZE]
                     [--zoom ZOOM] [--drop DROP] [--background BG]
                     [--target X Y Z] [--radius RADIUS] [--height HEIGHT]
                     [-o OUTPUT]
                     [source]

positional arguments

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
source.ply to render (default: newest export)

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
-s, --scene.scene folder (default: current folder)
--seconds12.0video length (default 12)
--size1920x1080video size WIDTHxHEIGHT (default 1920x1080)
--zoom1.3orbit radius times the median camera distance (default 1.3)
--drop0.35aim this far below the centre, in splat units (default 0.35)
--background#rrggbb, `jutaka` (the public-art viewer's sky), or 'linear-gradient(to bottom, rgb(r,g,b) P%%, ...)' (default: SuperSplat's background); a gradient renders twice and blends with ffmpeg
--targetorbit this point (splat coordinates) instead of the cameras' centre
--radiusorbit radius in splat units (overrides --zoom)
--heightcamera height above the target in splat units (default: the cameras' median)
-o, --outputwrite the video here instead of runs/orbit/<time>/orbit.mp4

gausser align

move a splat into the coordinate frame of a published one

Estimate the similarity (scale, rotation, translation) that maps MOVING's opaque splat centres onto the --to splat(s), and write MOVING moved by it, so camera presets and geometry made for the published splat fit. REFERENCE is anything splat-transform reads (.ply, .sog, LOD child meta.json; several are concatenated) and may be a cropped or cleaned part of MOVING. Needs no scene.

gausser align [-h] --to REFERENCE [REFERENCE ...] [--no-scale]
                     -o OUTPUT
                     MOVING

positional arguments

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
MOVING.ply to move (a Brush export)

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
--topublished splat(s)
--no-scaleTrueestimate rotation and translation only
-o, --outputaligned .ply to write

gausser crop

keep training and meshing to a box around the subject

Set the box `train` and `mesh` keep to (sparse/crop.json): Brush starts only from points in it, its exports keep only splats in it, and the mesh is cut to it before refining. The box is in the model's level frame (up = +y); draw it in `gausser monitor` (3D tab, crop) and paste the command it shows. Write negative numbers as --box=-1,0,-1,1,2,1. A new crop makes train and mesh out of date; a new solve drops it. Without options: show the crop.

gausser crop [-h] [-s SCENE] [--box x,y,z,X,Y,Z] [--up x,y,z] [--clear]

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
-s, --scene.scene folder (default: current folder)
--boxminimum and maximum corner, level frame
--upthe model's up the box was drawn with (default: computed)
--clearremove the crop

gausser monitor

watch the scene in a web page: steps, logs, COLMAP cameras, splats

Open the scene in the read-only web monitor on 127.0.0.1, starting the monitor unless it runs. One monitor serves every scene gausser has worked on; it shows a running command live and works as a viewer afterwards. `--monitor` on run, frames, mask, solve, train and lod starts it in the background.

gausser monitor [-h] [-s SCENE] [--all] [--port PORT] [--no-open]

options

optionchoicesdefaultmeaning
-h, --helpshow this help message and exit
-s, --scene.scene folder (default: current folder)
--allopen the list of all scenes
--port8737port of a new monitor (default 8737)
--no-opendo not open a browser
